newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA - SHARES EASE IN LIGHT TRADE, GAINS SEEN.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA - SHARES EASE IN LIGHT TRADE, GAINS SEEN.

text.p: Lithuanian shares eased slightly in light trade on Monday but dealers said that they expected prices to rise again soon.
The Litin A index dipped 6.82 points to 2,562.17 in central market trade of just under 512,000 litas.
Monday also marked the debut of the official list and its index, which was launched at 1,000.
The list is comprised of four blue chip companies: cardboard maker Medienos Plaushas, Rokishkis Cheese, Vilniaus Bank and Hermis Bank.

Hermis Bank was one of the session's few gainers, advancing to 191.00 litas from 190.00 litas in trade of 30,560 litas. Vilniaus Bank remained unchanged at 250.00 litas and none of its shares changed hands.
Medienos Plaushas was unmoved at 14.00 litas in trade of almost 29,000 litas while Rokishkis Cheese edged up to 47.00 litas from 46.00 litas and trade in its shares reached over 98,000 litas.
Losers included the Lithuania Sea Shipping Company, which dipped to 8.20 litas from 8.49 litas in trade of 16,400 litas.
Dealers said they anticipated prices and activity to pick up now that a number of short-term investors had bailed with dividends in hand.
"More long-term investors are coming to the market now and that should help to boost prices," one dealer said.
Block trades reached over 1.4 million litas and the secondary T-bill market turned over 40,100 litas.
Dealers said they expect the secondary T-bill market to pick up after the central bank begins repo auctions, which could start at the end of April.
The secondary T-bill market was relatively active this time last year when yields on the primary market soared in the wake of a banking crisis.
But yields have been comparatively low since last fall, when the government successfully tapped the international capital markets with a syndicated loan on favourable conditions.
